headline: Quiet Bats Cost Red Sox A Sweep In Frustrating Seattle Finale
morning_brew: We had the sweep right there in our hands out in Seattle, but the bats went completely quiet in a frustrating three to one loss. Payton Tolle didn't pitch terribly, giving up three runs over six innings, but you aren't winning many ballgames when your lineup only musters five hits. Nate Eaton provided the only spark of the afternoon with a solo home run in the third, but after that, the offense went completely flat. It's just agonizing to watch this team tease us with a couple of nice wins only to spit the bit when they have a chance to build some real momentum.

I haven't seen an offense look this helpless since my cousin Jimmy tried to hit cleanup for his beer-league softball team and ended up pulling a hamstring during a practice swing. Outside of Eaton's blast, we couldn't get anything going, and Willson Contreras going zero for four at the top of the card didn't help matters. Now we have to dust ourselves off and head into Colorado for a three-game series starting tonight. We're sitting at thirty-one and forty-four, dead last in the division, and we need to start stacking wins fast before the Yankees come to Fenway later this week.

Down in Foxborough, the chatter is shifting to offseason standouts as we get closer to training camp, and we're all hoping a few of these young wideouts can make a massive leap for Drake Maye. Over on the ice, the B's are gearing up for the draft later this week, though the real excitement is already locked in for next year when they finally raise Patrice Bergeron's number thirty-seven to the rafters. That's a well-deserved honor for the ultimate captain, but right now, I need the Sox to show some life at Coors Field tonight.
